readme.title: Career workbook
lines: This workbook holds your career data: jobs, studies, achievements and skills,
plus the roles you aim for, the jobs you apply to and the sources the AI uses when you ask it to search.
The AI reads it to write each CV, and keeps it up to date with you.
You can also edit it yourself at any time.
## How it works
Each sheet is a table, and each row is one thing: a job, a degree, an achievement, a skill.
Every row needs an ID in the first column, and no two rows can share one:
E1, E2, ... in Experience & Education       A1, A2, ... in Achievements & Responsibilities
S1, S2, ... in Skills                       R1, R2, ... in Target Roles
J1, J2, ... in Application Tracker          F1, F2, ... in Finder Sources
Never change or reuse an ID: each line of a CV points to the row it comes from by its ID.
## IDs link the sheets
Where (in Achievements) holds the ID of the job or study it belongs to, for example E2.
Evidence (in Skills) holds the IDs of the achievements that show the skill, for example A1, A4.
Key skills (in Target Roles) holds skill IDs, for example S1, S3.
## Only verified achievements reach a CV
An achievement can appear in a CV only when Verified = Yes.
Mark it only when the wording is true and you can back it up in an interview.
Nothing in a CV is invented: if it is not in this workbook, it is not in the CV.
## Please do not
Rename, delete or reorder the sheets, or change the column titles: the AI finds them by name.
Put two things in one row, or leave a row without an ID.
## Tips
Dates look like 2023-02-01. For something current, leave End empty and set Current = Yes.
Columns with an arrow have a list of options. Point at a column title to see what goes there.
Use the filter buttons on the first row to sort or find rows.

columns.name: ID
columns.note: Unique ID of the row: E1, E2, ... Never reuse or change it.

columns.name: Name
columns.note: Job title, degree, certification or project, exactly as officially held.

columns.name: Organization
columns.note: Company, school or issuer, with its official name.

columns.name: English title
columns.note: The same title in English, if it has an official or common one.

columns.name: End
columns.note: Leave it empty if it is current.

columns.name: Current
columns.note: Yes if you are still doing it.

columns.name: Location / work mode
columns.note: City and country, and on-site, hybrid or remote.

columns.name: Summary
columns.note: What you did there, in your own words. The AI reads it as the page of this row.

columns.name: Link / credential
columns.note: Credential ID or verification link, if any.

columns.name: ID
columns.note: Unique ID of the row: A1, A2, ... Never reuse or change it.

columns.name: Description
columns.note: One line: what you did or achieved.

columns.name: Where (experience ID)
columns.note: The ID of the job or study in Experience & Education, for example E2.

columns.name: Skills shown (skill IDs, comma-separated)
columns.note: Skill IDs from the Skills sheet, for example S1, S4.

columns.name: Metric / result
columns.note: The number or result, if there is one: 15% less rework, 60 claims a day.

columns.name: Context (STAR)
columns.note: Situation, task, action and result, for interviews.

columns.name: Verified
columns.note: Yes only when the wording is true and you can back it up. Only verified achievements can appear in a CV.

columns.name: ID
columns.note: Unique ID of the row: S1, S2, ... Never reuse or change it.

columns.name: Evidence (achievement IDs)
columns.note: Achievement IDs that show this skill, for example A1, A4.

columns.name: Synonyms / how job posts ask for it

columns.note: From 0 to 100.
